steps.determines: CHOSEN (a witness configuration; UNIQUE up to icosahedral symmetry)
steps.what: the twelve icosahedral vertices -- the kissing witness
steps.why: the twelve candidate sphere-centers are the regular-icosahedron vertices, in golden-ratio coordinates -- twelve distinct points, the even cyclic images of (0,1,phi) with all sign choices. This is the WITNESS that kissing number >= 12; it lives in the Euclidean 3-space the bridge (05) provides.

steps.expr: |v|^2 = 2 + phi for all twelve (using phi^2 = phi + 1)
steps.what: equidistant from the center -- every vertex has norm^2 = 2 + phi = R^2
steps.why: each vertex is the same distance R from the origin: |(0,1,phi)|^2 = 1 + phi^2 = 2 + phi, and likewise for all twelve by symmetry. So the twelve centers lie on one sphere of radius R -- the precondition for kissing a central sphere. Exact in Z[phi].

steps.determines: UNIQUE (the distance multiset is fixed by the configuration)
steps.expr: pairwise dist^2 in {4, 4+4phi, 8+4phi}; min = 4 (the icosahedron edge)
steps.what: three pairwise distance classes {4, 4+4phi, 8+4phi}; the minimum is the edge
steps.why: the 66 vertex pairs take exactly three squared distances: 4 (the 30 edges), 4+4phi (the off-edges), and 8+4phi (the 6 antipodal pairs). The MINIMUM pairwise distance^2 is 4, the edge -- this is what must clear R^2 for the spheres not to overlap. All exact in Z[phi].

steps.check: every dist^2 > R^2; the edge gap 2 - phi > 0 reduces to 5 < 9
steps.determines: UNIQUE (the kissing configuration exists; kissing number >= 12)
steps.expr: dist^2 - R^2 > 0 for all three classes; the tightest, 4 - (2+phi) = 2 - phi, is > 0 <=> 5 < 9
steps.what: THE KISSING -- every pairwise distance^2 exceeds R^2 (reduces to 5 < 9)
steps.why: for the twelve spheres (radius R/2) to kiss the central one without overlapping, every pairwise distance must be at least R -- i.e. every dist^2 - R^2 >= 0. The two large gaps (2+3phi, 6+3phi) are positive because phi > 0; the tightest, the EDGE, gives 4 - (2+phi) = 2 - phi, and 2 - phi > 0 <=> phi < 2 <=> 1 + sqrt5 < 4 <=> sqrt5 < 3 <=> 5 < 9. So the whole kissing result bottoms out at exact Z[phi] arithmetic plus the integer fact 5 < 9. The inequality is STRICT -- the twelve spheres rattle, they do not touch each other.

steps.determines: the reading (12 achieved; saturation is the central OWED), held
steps.expr: kissing >= 12 (built); kissing = 12 and 'why exactly 12' point beyond
steps.what: the reading -- 12 is achieved; whether the substrate SATURATES at 12 is the deep OWED
steps.why: the icosahedral twelve is the kissing witness, built. Whether REGISTRATION forces exactly twelve mutual adjacencies -- the SATURATION -- is the framework's central number: it is container 01's OWED (1.6, adjacency -> 12) and the phase cycle -> 12, and it is EQUIVALENT to the dim=3 upper bound (12 is the maximum kissing number only in 3-D: d=2 caps at 6, d=4 reaches 24). So dim=3 should FALL OUT of why-12, not be attacked head-on. Held as the reading.

steps.expr: no 13 equal spheres kiss a central one in 3-D (kissing(3) = 12)
steps.what: the upper bound (kissing = 12, no 13th) -- external / OWED
steps.why: the >= 12 half is built here. The <= 12 half -- that no 13th sphere fits -- is Schuette-van der Waerden 1953, EXTERNAL accepted mathematics, NOT machine-checked in this repo (a formalization far beyond reasonable effort). Cited, not claimed as our THEOREM; same tier as maths 4's KISSING-UPPER-BOUND-EXTERNAL. Together with 6.4 it gives kissing(3) = 12, the >= half ours and the <= half on citation.
